symbols.name: Gye Nyame
symbols.summary: Expresses the omnipotence and supremacy of God; the most popular Adinkra in Ghana, featured on the 200-cedi note and several university crests.

symbols.name: Sankofa (Bird)
symbols.summary: Wisdom of learning from the past to build the future; shown as a mythical bird moving forward while looking back with an egg in its beak. Most popular Adinkra in the African diaspora.

symbols.name: Sankofa (Heart)
symbols.summary: Alternative stylized-heart form of Sankofa; the spirals represent returning to one's roots to draw lessons for the present and future.

symbols.name: Adinkrahene
symbols.summary: Symbol of authority, leadership and charisma; its concentric circles are said to have inspired the design of all other Adinkra.

symbols.name: Dwennimmen
symbols.summary: Strength of mind, body and soul combined with humility, wisdom and learning; featured in the University of Ghana logo.

symbols.name: Funtumfunefu Denkyemfunefu
symbols.summary: Unity in diversity and a common destiny; from the proverb of two crocodiles who share one stomach yet still fight over food.

symbols.name: Nkyinkyim
symbols.summary: Represents the tortuous nature of life's journey and the toughness, versatility, dynamism and dedication needed to thrive in it.

symbols.name: Odo Nnyew Fie Kwan
symbols.literal_meaning: Love does not lose its way home
symbols.summary: Those who are led by love always end up in the right place.

symbols.name: Denkyem
symbols.summary: Symbol of adaptability and cleverness.

symbols.name: Nea Onnim
symbols.summary: Knowledge and life-long learning; from the proverb that when the ignorant one learns, he comes to know.

symbols.name: Nsoromma
symbols.summary: Faith and belief in patronage by, and dependency on, a supreme being.

symbols.name: Aban
symbols.summary: Strength, seat of power, authority and magnificence.

symbols.name: Abe Dua
symbols.summary: Wealth, resourcefulness and self-sufficiency.

symbols.name: Abode Santann
symbols.summary: The vast expanse of natural and social creation by God; combines the eye, sun rays, double crescent moon and stool to depict divine and human creativity.

symbols.name: Abusua Pa
symbols.summary: Family unity, kinship ties and support; 'it is in a good family that love and unity exist.'

symbols.name: Adwo
symbols.summary: Peace, tranquility and quiet.

symbols.name: Agyin Dawuru
symbols.summary: Faithfulness, alertness and dutifulness; commemorates Agyin, the loyal gong-beater of the Asantehene.

symbols.name: Akoben
symbols.summary: A call to action, readiness and voluntarism.

symbols.name: Akofena
symbols.literal_meaning: Sword of war / state ceremonial sword
symbols.summary: State authority, legality and legitimized rule; recognition of gallantry. Appears on Ghana's coat of arms.

symbols.name: Akoko Nan
symbols.summary: Discipline coupled with care and nurturing; proverb: the hen's foot steps on the chick but does not kill it.

symbols.name: Akoma Ntoaso
symbols.summary: Agreement, togetherness, unity and charter; an amplification of the Akoma (heart) concept.

symbols.name: Akoma
symbols.summary: Love, goodwill, patience, faithfulness, fondness, endurance and consistency.

symbols.name: Ananse Ntentan
symbols.summary: Wisdom, craftiness, creativity and the complexities of life; the web of Ananse, the clever spider of African folklore.

symbols.name: Ani Bere A Enso Gya
symbols.literal_meaning: Red eyes do not spark flames
symbols.summary: Patience, self-containment, self-discipline and self-control no matter how serious one becomes.

symbols.name: Anyi Me Aye A
symbols.literal_meaning: If you will not praise me
symbols.summary: Warns against ingratitude and boorishness: 'if you will not praise me, do not spoil my name.'

symbols.name: Aponkyerene Wu A
symbols.summary: Significance and value; 'it is when a frog dies that we see its true length' — we undervalue things until we lose them.

symbols.name: Asaawa
symbols.summary: Sweetness, pleasure and hedonism; proverb: sweetness does not stay in the mouth forever.

symbols.name: Asase Ye Duru
symbols.summary: Providence and the divinity of Mother Earth.

symbols.name: Asetena Pa
symbols.summary: Conspicuous spending, indulgence, wealth and upper social class; 'good living makes one forget his humble beginnings.'

symbols.name: Aya
symbols.summary: Endurance, independence, defiance against difficulties, hardiness, perseverance and resourcefulness.

symbols.name: Bese Saka
symbols.summary: Affluence, power, abundance and plenty; also togetherness and unity.

symbols.name: Bi Nka Bi
symbols.literal_meaning: Let no one bite the other
symbols.summary: Justice, fair play, freedom, peace, forgiveness, unity, harmony and the avoidance of conflict.

symbols.name: Boa Me Na Me Mmoa Wo
symbols.literal_meaning: Help me and let me help you
symbols.summary: Cooperation and interdependence; like the left hand washing the right and vice versa.

symbols.name: Boafo Ye Na
symbols.summary: Support, patronage, cooperation and teamwork; highlights the rarity of a willing helper.

symbols.name: Dame Dame
symbols.summary: Craftiness, intelligence and strategy.

symbols.name: Dono Ntoaso
symbols.summary: United action, alertness, goodwill, praise, rejoicing and adroitness.

symbols.name: Dono
symbols.summary: Appellation, praise, goodwill and rhythm.

symbols.name: Duafe
symbols.summary: Feminine consideration and good feminine qualities: patience, prudence, fondness, love and care.

symbols.name: Dwantire
symbols.summary: Innocence and guiltlessness; the guiltless fears no accusation, hence the ram is always in white.

symbols.name: Eban
symbols.summary: Safety, security and love.

symbols.name: Epa
symbols.summary: Law and justice.

symbols.name: Ese ne Tekrema
symbols.summary: Improvement, advancement, growth and the need for friendliness and interdependence.

symbols.name: Esono Anantam
symbols.summary: Leadership, protection, power and security; 'when you follow the elephant, the dew does not wet you.'

symbols.name: Fafanto
symbols.summary: Tenderness, gentleness, honesty and fragility.

symbols.name: Fawohodie
symbols.summary: Emancipation, self-determination and self-government; proverb: freedom walks with suffering, i.e. it comes with responsibilities.

symbols.name: Fihankra
symbols.summary: Brotherhood, safety, security, completeness and solidarity.

symbols.name: Fofo
symbols.summary: A warning against jealousy and covetousness.

symbols.name: Gyawu Atiko
symbols.summary: Valor and bravery; used interchangeably with Kwatakye Atiko.

symbols.name: Hwehwemudua
symbols.summary: Excellence, superior quality, perfection, knowledge and critical examination.

symbols.name: Hye Wo Nhye
symbols.summary: Toughness, imperishability and permanence.

symbols.name: Kete Pa
symbols.summary: Good and successful marriage and good care; a woman in a good marriage is placed on a good bed.

symbols.name: Kokuromotie
symbols.summary: Cooperation, participation, teamwork, indispensability and harmony; 'we don't bypass the thumb to tie a knot.'

symbols.name: Kramo Bone Amma Yeanhu Kramo Pa
symbols.literal_meaning: The bad Muslim makes it hard to recognize the good one
symbols.summary: A warning against deception and hypocrisy.

symbols.name: Krapa
symbols.literal_meaning: Good soul / thing that removes filth or evil
symbols.summary: Spiritual balance, good fortune, luck, sanctity, spiritual strength and uprightness of spirit.

symbols.name: Kuronti ne Akwamu
symbols.summary: Democracy, sharing of ideas and taking counsel.

symbols.name: Kwatakye Atiko
symbols.summary: Valor and bravery; the hairstyle of Kwatakye, a war captain of old Asante. Also called Gyawu Atiko.

symbols.name: Kyemfere
symbols.summary: Knowledge, experience, service, keepsake, antiquity, rarity and heirloom; proverb: the potsherd claims age, but what of the potter?

symbols.name: Mako
symbols.summary: Inequality and uneven development; peppers on the same plant do not ripen at the same time.

symbols.name: Mate Masie
symbols.literal_meaning: I have heard and kept it
symbols.summary: Wisdom, knowledge and prudence; 'the hole of wisdom is I have heard and kept it.'

symbols.name: Mekyea Wo
symbols.summary: Greetings, recognition and respect; to greet is to acknowledge a fellow human being.

symbols.name: Menso Wo Kenten
symbols.literal_meaning: I am not carrying your basket
symbols.summary: Industry, self-reliance and economic self-determination.

symbols.name: Mframadan
symbols.summary: Resilience and readiness to face the vicissitudes of life.

symbols.name: Mmeramubere
symbols.summary: Warmth, sunshine and vitality.

symbols.name: Mmeramutene
symbols.summary: Sunlight, warmth, endurance and uprightness.

symbols.name: Mmere Dane
symbols.summary: The temporariness of good times; change and transition.

symbols.name: Mpatapo
symbols.summary: Pacification, forgiveness and reconciliation.

symbols.name: Mpuannum
symbols.summary: Loyalty and priestly office.

symbols.name: Nea Ope Se Obedi Hene
symbols.literal_meaning: He who wants to be a king
symbols.summary: Leadership qualities and service; 'he who wants to be king in the future begins by learning how to serve.'

symbols.name: Nea Oretwa Sa
symbols.summary: Trailblazing leadership and its blind spots; the paver does not see the crooked path behind him, so a leader must heed advice.

symbols.name: Nkonsonkonson
symbols.summary: Unity and community; the bonds that hold people together.

symbols.name: Nkotimsefo Mpua
symbols.summary: Loyalty and readiness to serve.

symbols.name: Nkrabea
symbols.summary: Destiny, determinism and the unequal distribution of talents; 'God's destiny cannot be circumvented.'

symbols.name: Nkyemu
symbols.summary: The grid stamped on cloth before symbols are printed; adroitness, precision and quality craftsmanship.

symbols.name: Nnamfo Pa Baanu
symbols.summary: Friendship, fellowship and comradeship; 'thinking is done in pairs.'

symbols.name: Nsaa
symbols.summary: Excellence, genuineness and authenticity, after a cloth renowned for its quality.

symbols.name: Nserewa
symbols.summary: Affluence and wealth, and sacredness in priestly use; cowries were pre-colonial money and gave the cedi its name.

symbols.name: Nteasee
symbols.summary: Understanding and cooperation.

symbols.name: Nyame Baatanpa
symbols.summary: The caring and nurturing of God over all His creation.

symbols.name: Nyame Biribi Wo Soro
symbols.literal_meaning: God, there is something in the heavens
symbols.summary: Hope and inspiration; 'let that good thing up there come to me.'

symbols.name: Nyame Dua
symbols.summary: God's presence and protection; the sacred stump kept in Akan homes for rituals.

symbols.name: Nyame Nti
symbols.literal_meaning: Because of God / by God's grace
symbols.summary: Faith and trust in God; 'by God's grace I will not feed on leaves like an animal.'

symbols.name: Nyame Nwu Na Mawu
symbols.literal_meaning: God won't die for me to die
symbols.summary: Expresses the immortality of the human soul and faith in God's sustaining power.

symbols.name: Nyansapo
symbols.summary: Wisdom, ingenuity, intelligence and patience; 'a wisdom knot is untied only by the wise.' Used in the KNUST logo and motto.

symbols.name: Obohemaa
symbols.summary: Preciousness, gem and treasure; warns against spending money on worthless stones.

symbols.name: Ohene Aniwa
symbols.summary: Vigilance, far-sightedness, intelligence, protection and authority; 'the king's eyes surround him.'

symbols.name: Okodee Mmowere
symbols.summary: Strength, bravery and power, drawn from the character of the eagle.

symbols.name: Okuafo Pa
symbols.summary: Diligence, hard work and entrepreneurship.

symbols.name: Osram ne Nsoromma
symbols.summary: Faithfulness, fondness, harmony, benevolence, love, loyalty and femininity.

symbols.name: Owo Foro Adobe
symbols.literal_meaning: A snake climbs a raffia palm
symbols.summary: Ingenuity, excellence and the performance of feats; achieving the unusual or impossible.

symbols.name: Owuo Atwedee
symbols.summary: The certainty and universality of death; all must climb this ladder.

symbols.name: Pempamsie
symbols.summary: Foresight, readiness, steadfastness, hardiness, valor and fearlessness.

symbols.name: Sepow
symbols.summary: Justice; the knife used to execute those condemned by law.

symbols.name: Sesa Wo Suban
symbols.summary: A warning against arrogance, bad manners and dishonorable behavior; calls for self-reformation.

symbols.name: Som Onyankopon
symbols.summary: Devotion and worship of the Supreme Being.

symbols.name: Sunsum
symbols.summary: Spiritual purity and cleanliness of soul; believed to be the part of God transmitted to a person through the father, distinct from the mother's blood.

symbols.name: Tabono
symbols.summary: Strength, confidence and persistence, drawn from the qualities needed to paddle a boat.

symbols.name: Tamfo Bebre
symbols.literal_meaning: The enemy will stew in his own juice
symbols.summary: Ill-will, jealousy and envy; the enemy suffers from his own schemes.

symbols.name: UAC Nkanea
symbols.summary: Technological advancement and modernity, named after the lights of the United Africa Company.

symbols.name: Wawa Aba
symbols.summary: Hardiness, toughness and perseverance.

symbols.name: Wo Nsa Da Mu A
symbols.literal_meaning: When your hands are inside (the dish)
symbols.summary: Participatory government, democracy and pluralism; 'when your hands are in the dish, people don't eat everything and leave you nothing.'

symbols.name: Woforo Dua Pa A
symbols.literal_meaning: When you climb a good tree
symbols.summary: Support for good causes; those who climb a good tree are helped by others.
